subject: Commercial model: seat vs node bundle for private deployment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellison <t.ellison@acmeretail.com>, Amy Park <amy.park@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: seat vs node bundle for Acme private deployment

Hi Tom / Amy,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — attaching a concise commercial proposal so you can review with procurement and engineering. Two packaging options we think map well to Acme's use case (high steady inference, seasonal peaks):

1) Seat-based bundle (recommended for dev + predictable internal tooling):
- Per-seat license for model access (concurrent seats capped), includes per-seat KV cache allocation and developer tooling.
- Platform fee: amortized monthly, covers control plane, telemetry, and encryption integrations.
- Support: Silver (business hours) included; Gold (24/7) optional.

2) Node-hours bundle (recommended for large inference volumes):
- Node-hour pool (GPU hours) with priority routing and dedicated node reservation during business hours.
- Lower per-token economics at scale; platform fee applied as a %-of-commit credit.

Key points and asks:
- We can offer a 1.5 - 2 year commit structure to lock lower unit pricing.
- Migration credit and 30% reduced platform fee in year 1 for a 2-year commitment on node-hours.
- Need clarity on expected average tokens/sec and peak concurrency to finalize the SKU mix.

Attached: term-sheet-acme-20260821.pdf (commercial grid) and SOW-Acme-v1.docx (services/delivery).

Could you confirm: target commit (months/years), expected average qps, and whether you prefer a seat or node consumption model? Once we have that I can circulate a redline-ready term sheet.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: seat vs node bundle for Acme private deployment

Marissa — appreciate the clear options. A few follow-ups from procurement and cloud ops: 

- Commercial: can you do a steeper discount for a 3-year commit vs 2-year? Procurement is pushing for ~25% off list on the node-hour model if we commit to a baseline.
- Platform fee: can that be capped and amortized across our multi-account deploys? We want predictable OPEX rather than a % swing.
- Support: we need 24/7 on-call for our payment/checkout stack — is Gold mandatory for that, and what are response targets?
- Services: one weekend onsite for initial cutover — what's day rate and included deliverables?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposal: seat vs node bundle for Acme — procurement asks

Ben / Laura — forwarding Acme's procurement questions. Highlights: they asked for 25% off with a 3-year commit, a capped platform fee amortized across accounts, 24/7 on-call for payments stack, and one onsite weekend for cutover.

My read: Acme is strategic (large retail account, potential multi-region expansion). We can probably go deeper on discount if we ask for stronger baseline throughput commitment and a formal SLO/Rollout window. Options to consider:
- Trade deeper discount (18%–20%) for 2-year firm + 8% prepay (upfront) OR 22% for 3-year with annual true-up.
- Offer platform fee cap (fixed monthly) in exchange for minimum monthly node-hour commit.
- Offer Gold support for 24/7 but add an escalation SLA for payment-critical endpoints with a higher severity response SLA.
- Onsite day rate: suggest $4,200/day standard, with first weekend included as part of a migration credit for a 2-year commit.

Attaching internal-concessions-notes.txt with a quick matrix. Can you both review and confirm acceptable concession thresholds so I can send a counter?

—Marissa
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposal: seat vs node bundle for Acme — procurement asks

Marissa / Laura — quick recommended approach based on ARR plan and platform utilization: 

1) Commercial structure (recommended):
- 2-year firm commit on node-hours with an optional 3rd year renewal at pre-agreed uplift.
- Pricing: 18% off list for 2-year paid annually; 22% off for 3-year paid annually (or 20% + 8% upfront credit).
- Platform fee: convert to a fixed monthly cap tied to tier (Starter / Growth / Enterprise) and include a credit in month 1 equal to 30% of first quarter platform fees as migration credit.

2) Support & SLA:
- Gold support (24/7) available; payment-critical endpoints get Priority+ escalation (30-minute phone ack, 2-hour remediation target for severity 1).
- Onsite: include first weekend (2 days) as part of migration credit; additional days at $4,000/day.

3) Negotiation levers to protect unit economics:
- Annual true-ups on committed node-hours (if usage exceeds commit, overage at discounted rate; if under, apply rollforward credits up to 3 months).
- Technical validation window: require a run-rate report after 90 days to optimize batch/quantization to hit target economics.

If Acme wants 25% flat for 3 years we'd require either a material prepay (25% upfront) or a minimum annualized spend guarantee + penalty. I recommend we open with the 18%/22% bands and the fixed platform fee cap language. Laura — if you're comfortable, I can draft the redline to term-sheet-acme.

—Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Tom Ellison <t.ellison@acmeretail.com>

Marissa / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the suggested concessions. Procurement has reviewed and we can accept the 18% discount for a 2-year firm commit with the following conditions:

- Platform fee must be capped and amortized monthly as proposed.
- Priority+ escalation for payment-critical endpoints must be included in the contract appendix.
- SOC2 evidence and network diagrams to be provided before PO; security team will validate the controls.
- Please send an updated term-sheet and a DocuSign-ready contract; we will aim to issue PO within two weeks after security sign-off.
